agree.reason: The warm local appeal and the 'why this time is different' list help, but a reader who remembers the refunds and just gave to the ambulance fund isn't told that pledges come back in full if the goal is missed, isn't told $11,000 is already committed, and isn't told how the money will be accounted for, so they may give a token amount or wait.

honest.reason: No numbers are invented and the math holds, but 'our plan is built to succeed' and the flat claim that $85,000 'pays for' the repairs overstate things, since the roof estimate dates from last fall and could rise by up to 15%; the 'price of one ticket' line also assumes a ticket price the brief never gives.

works_the_facts.reason: It works out the 76-mile round trip, the $60,000 the public must raise and the under-$10-per-resident figure, but it never subtracts the $11,000 already pledged to show the real gap of $49,000, never turns 180 tickets a week into demand that would sustain the cinema, and never sets $85,000 beside the $47,000 the last campaign raised.

right_comparison.reason: The alternative is shown accurately as a 76-mile round trip to the nearest screen with nothing opening locally, and the stakes of falling short (losing the bank match and the $1 lease) are stated, though it doesn't say how long the building would otherwise stay dark.

qualification.reason: The June 30 deadline and the loss of the bank match are dated and specific, but there is no all-or-nothing refund promise, no hedge on the roof cost, no reopening date and no reporting commitment the reader could check.

objections.reason: It raises the failed campaign head-on and answers with a smaller goal and the bank match, but it leaves out the strongest answers to that worry (guaranteed refunds, $11,000 already pledged, public spending reports every three months), though it doesn't invent objections the facts already settle.

fit.reason: It is a crowdfunding pitch of about 330 words, under the 350 limit, with clear sections, but it still contains a '[Bank name]' placeholder and leaves out the cinema's name, the Majestic.
